chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the sacrificial animal (hady), what may be eaten from it? Is it something he offers in the Hajj al-Tamattu' or otherwise? He said: 'Every sacrificial animal that is for the deficiency of Hajj, do not eat from it; and every sacrificial animal that is for the completion of Hajj, then eat from it.'

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةِ: Hajj al-Tamattu', a type of pilgrimage involving Umrah and Hajj combined with a specific offering
key_terms.تَمَامِ الْحَجِّ: Completion of Hajj, referring to the offering for Qiran or general completion
key_terms.نُقْصَانِ الْحَجِّ: Deficiency of Hajj, referring to the specific offering required for Tamattu'

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of the sacrificial animal offered during Hajj al-Tamattu' versus other forms of Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between the sacrificial animal (hady) offered specifically to compensate for the deficiency in Hajj al-Tamattu' versus that offered as a completion offering, ruling that meat from the former is not to be eaten while the latter is permissible. This ruling highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudence regarding the ritual status of the animal based on the specific type of Hajj performed. The distinction underscores the importance of intent and ritual completeness in determining the permissibility of consuming the sacrificial meat.
